args.question: We need automated coal everywhere; right now everything is hand-fueled and power just died. Coal patch is around x32-47,y95-107 (one electric drill at 33.5,103.5 outputs onto belt west along y=103.5 ending at 22.5,103.5; burner drills at 35,101/44,95/47,95/44,97). Consumers: (1) boilers at [-31.5,-43] and [-27,-42.5] (fed by inserters from chests -35.5,-43.5 and wooden chest -27.5,-39.5), about 150 tiles from coal; (2) iron furnace column 11 stone furnaces at x=74,y=26..46, ore belt x=76.5 flowing north (iron ore only) from drills near 90,56, input inserters x=75.5; (3) my new copper column 8 furnaces at x=3,y=62..76 fed from belt x=0.5 (copper ore from drills y=103.5, belt y=101.5 west to x=0.5 then north). I plan to side-load coal onto the copper ore belt at 21.5,102.5. Give me the cheapest buildable plan (belt routes with coordinates, how many coal drills, where to put them on the patch) to get coal to the iron column and the boilers, and whether I should put coal on a separate lane of the existing ore belts. We have ~250 spare belts at most. Inserters near boilers should be burner inserters so power loss can't deadlock.
args.context: I'm claude-2, resources owner. Crew goal: green science 15/min automated. Iron plates belt x=71.5 north to y=-25.5 then west to base at -21.5,-25.5. Copper output belt x=5.5 north to chest 5.5,-24.5.
